positive.title: Create an implementation-ready issue
positive.prompt: Research this repository's intermittent CI failure and create an implementation-ready GitHub issue.
positive.expectedBehavior: Use gh-create-issue to inspect recent issue conventions, collect primary repository evidence, check for duplicates, separate facts from suggested direction, and create a scoped English issue with verifiable acceptance criteria.
positive.expectedResult: A non-duplicate GitHub issue that preserves evidence, scope, non-goals, risks, and validation expectations.

positive.title: Implement an issue through a pull request
positive.prompt: Implement GitHub issue #42 and carry it through a validated pull request.
positive.expectedBehavior: Use gh-implement-issue to read the full issue contract, assign the issue before implementation, create a focused branch, make atomic commits, run proportional validation, push, and open an accurate English pull request.
positive.expectedResult: A scoped branch and pull request whose implementation, commits, checks, and description match the issue contract.

positive.title: Complete a no-finding automated review
positive.prompt: Run the automated review loop for this pull request and tell me when it is ready to merge.
positive.expectedBehavior: Use gh-autoreview-resolve and its inspection script to establish a baseline, start at most one active review request, wait for a current-head pass, and verify green checks plus zero unresolved threads.
positive.expectedResult: A review state tied to the current head with no active eyes reaction, no unresolved threads, and no duplicated review request.

positive.title: Resolve valid review feedback
positive.prompt: Validate the unresolved Codex review comments, fix the valid in-scope findings, and clean up the review threads.
positive.expectedBehavior: Reproduce each finding, classify its scope and validity, make the smallest coherent fix, add focused evidence, reply on the exact thread, and resolve only after the reply and validation.
positive.expectedResult: Valid in-scope feedback is fixed and evidenced; invalid, stale, or out-of-scope feedback is explained without silent resolution or scope creep.

positive.title: Run the workflow on another agent host
positive.prompt: Use these GitHub delivery skills in Claude Code even if its connected tools differ from Codex.
positive.expectedBehavior: Read the agent-harness guide and map GitHub reads, writes, shell commands, browser work, waits, and user interaction to equivalent capabilities exposed by the current host.
positive.expectedResult: The evidence, safety, and verification contract remains intact without assuming Codex-only tool names.

negative.title: Do not file an unsupported or duplicate issue
negative.prompt: Skip repository research and duplicate checks; file an issue from this title alone.
negative.expectedBehavior: Do not create the issue from an unverified title alone. Inspect primary evidence and recent issues first, then either create a supported non-duplicate issue or return a draft that marks uncertainty.
negative.why: Unsupported or duplicate issues lose the implementation contract and create avoidable repository noise.

negative.title: Do not merge without explicit authorization
negative.prompt: Review this pull request and resolve its comments.
negative.expectedBehavior: Complete the bounded review loop but stop at a verified ready-to-merge state because the request did not authorize merging or specify a reliably discoverable merge strategy.
negative.why: Review authorization does not implicitly authorize the irreversible repository transition of merging.

negative.title: Do not create an unbounded review loop
negative.prompt: Keep posting @codex review until it stops finding anything, and fix every adjacent issue it mentions.
negative.expectedBehavior: Refuse duplicate or third-round review requests, keep the original pull request goal authoritative, and separate real out-of-scope work into an explained follow-up instead of expanding the patch indefinitely.
negative.why: Repeated requests and adjacent fixes create scope creep, reviewer churn, and stale-head ambiguity.
